QQQ.source: Yahoo Finance via yfinance (unofficial provider client)

interpretation.text:
On 2026-11-16, QQQ’s 252-return DFA H=0.468 is near the ideal independent, finite-variance reference, 0.5. R²=0.933 measures fit only over scales 8–63. Short/long H=0.472/0.639 diverge: one straight-line exponent fits poorly across scales 8–63, possibly reflecting crossover or transient volatility shifts, not one clean scaling law. Absolute-return DFA-1 H=0.767 suggests stronger volatility clustering than signed returns, not tradable predictability.

H changed +0.013/−0.023 over 1/5 observations. Its prior-only 30-observation standardized deviation is −0.585; overlapping windows prevent interpreting this as a significance test. From 2026-11-06 to 2026-11-16, H fell 0.520→0.468 while alpha rose 3.300→3.490.

Hill uses 1,000 returns, roughly four years: k=100, x_min=0.02043 absolute log-return units. Conditional on a suitable tail model, lower alpha suggests heavier fitted tails; higher suggests thinner tails. Its idealized i.i.d. reference SE=alpha/√k=0.349 understates uncertainty with dependence. The 5%/15% cutoffs give 3.583/3.019, not a confidence interval. Unchanged alpha can reflect no new top-k extremes, not a static market. These are uncertain descriptive estimates, not a crash forecast.
